answer: A knoll is a vantage: high enough to see the whole field, too small to hide on. An inlet is the one gap in the coast where outside flow enters a closed system and the level actually changes. A dune is settlement over time, grain on grain, moved by every wind and still standing where it fell. This network is all three. Graders are the knoll, the only seat that can see an answer whole. Recruiting is the inlet, useless unless its flow reaches the shallows where panels starve. And the backlog is the dune: answers deposited, ungraded, waiting for enough climbers.
